prompts.title: Pattern Recognition Quiz
prompts.description: Learn when to apply common DSA patterns
prompts.prompt: Act as an SDE interview coach. Give me 5 medium LeetCode-style problems one at a time. After I describe my approach, tell me which pattern applies (two pointers, sliding window, hash map, BFS, DP, etc.) and what signals in the problem statement led to that pattern.

prompts.title: Complexity Analysis Drill
prompts.description: Practice Big-O analysis on code snippets
prompts.prompt: Quiz me on time and space complexity. Present a code snippet (array, tree, or graph algorithm). I will analyze Big-O. Then evaluate my answer, explain mistakes, and show the optimal approach if mine is suboptimal.

prompts.title: Two Pointers Deep Dive
prompts.prompt: Explain two pointers technique with 3 variants: opposite direction (sorted array), same direction (in-place removal), and fast-slow (cycle detection). For each, give one LeetCode example, pseudocode template, and common pitfalls.

prompts.title: Dynamic Programming Framework
prompts.prompt: Teach me your DP framework: (1) define state, (2) recurrence relation, (3) base cases, (4) iteration order, (5) space optimization. Then apply it to the Coin Change problem with a full walkthrough.

prompts.title: Graph Problem Mock
prompts.prompt: Give me a graph interview problem (BFS, DFS, topo sort, or union-find). Wait for my approach before giving hints. Evaluate my BFS/DFS choice, time/space complexity, and edge cases like disconnected graphs or cycles.

prompts.title: Process vs Thread
prompts.prompt: Explain processes vs threads vs coroutines. Cover memory isolation, context switching cost, shared memory, and when each is used in production systems. Give 3 interview follow-up questions with model answers.

prompts.title: Deadlock Conditions
prompts.prompt: Explain the four Coffman conditions for deadlock. For each condition, describe a prevention or avoidance strategy (mutex ordering, banker's algorithm, timeout). Include a real-world example from database or OS context.

prompts.title: Virtual Memory Explained
prompts.prompt: Explain virtual memory: paging, page tables, TLB, page faults, and demand paging. Walk through what happens on a memory access. Compare paging vs segmentation. Keep it interview-ready in under 5 minutes of reading.

prompts.title: Scheduling Algorithms
prompts.prompt: Compare CPU scheduling algorithms: FCFS, SJF, Priority, Round Robin, MLFQ. For each, state advantages, disadvantages, starvation risk, and average wait time behavior. Give a scenario where Round Robin beats SJF.

prompts.title: ACID Properties
prompts.prompt: Explain ACID properties with a bank transfer example. For each property (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability), describe how DBMS implements it (undo logs, constraints, isolation levels, WAL). Include one failure scenario per property.

prompts.title: Indexing Deep Dive
prompts.description: B-trees, hash indexes, and query optimization
prompts.prompt: Explain database indexing: B-tree vs hash index vs bitmap index. When does an index help vs hurt? Cover composite indexes, leftmost prefix rule, and covering indexes. Give an example query and explain EXPLAIN plan reading.

prompts.title: Isolation Levels
prompts.prompt: Explain dirty read, non-repeatable read, and phantom read. Map each to SQL isolation levels (Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable). Recommend isolation level for an e-commerce inventory system.

prompts.title: Normalization Quiz
prompts.prompt: Teach normalization from 1NF to BCNF with a student-course-instructor example table. Show denormalized table, functional dependencies, and step-by-step decomposition. Explain when denormalization is acceptable in production.

prompts.title: TCP vs UDP
prompts.prompt: Compare TCP and UDP: connection setup, reliability, ordering, flow control, congestion control, use cases. Explain TCP 3-way handshake and 4-way teardown. When would you choose UDP for a production system?

prompts.title: HTTP & REST Design
prompts.description: HTTP methods, status codes, REST best practices
prompts.prompt: Explain HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3 at a high level. Cover idempotent methods, status code categories, and REST API design best practices. Design REST endpoints for a todo app with proper HTTP verbs and status codes.

prompts.title: DNS Resolution Walkthrough
prompts.description: What happens when you type a URL
prompts.prompt: Walk through DNS resolution step by step when a user types https://example.com. Cover browser cache, OS cache, recursive resolver, root/TLD/authoritative nameservers. Then explain DNS caching TTL and CDN interaction.

prompts.title: OSI vs TCP/IP Model
prompts.prompt: Compare OSI 7-layer and TCP/IP 4-layer models. For each layer, name key protocols and devices. Explain where SSL/TLS fits. Give one interview question per layer with a concise model answer.

prompts.title: SOLID Principles
prompts.prompt: Explain all 5 SOLID principles with a simple e-commerce code example for each. Show a violation and the refactored solution. Keep examples in pseudocode or TypeScript.

prompts.title: Inheritance vs Composition
prompts.description: When to favor composition over inheritance
prompts.prompt: Explain inheritance vs composition with examples. When is inheritance appropriate vs an anti-pattern? Cover the Liskov Substitution Principle. Refactor a fragile base class hierarchy into composition.

prompts.title: Design Patterns Overview
prompts.prompt: Summarize 6 essential design patterns for SDE interviews: Singleton, Factory, Observer, Strategy, Decorator, and Adapter. For each, state problem solved, structure, and one real-world use case.

prompts.title: Abstraction & Polymorphism
prompts.prompt: Explain the four OOP pillars: encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism. Use a payment processing system example. Include compile-time vs runtime polymorphism with code snippets.

prompts.title: Design Parking Lot
prompts.prompt: Help me design a Parking Lot system (LLD). Guide me through requirements clarification, class identification, relationships, and key methods. Cover multiple vehicle types, parking spots, floors, and payment. Use UML-style class descriptions.

prompts.title: Design LRU Cache
prompts.prompt: Walk me through LLD for an LRU Cache with O(1) get and put. Identify classes, data structures, and method signatures. Explain why HashMap + Doubly Linked List works. Cover thread-safety as a follow-up.

prompts.title: Design Rate Limiter
prompts.prompt: Guide me through designing a Rate Limiter (LLD). Compare token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window, and sliding window. Recommend one for an API gateway. Define classes, interfaces, and configuration options.

prompts.title: Design BookMyShow
prompts.prompt: Help me design a movie ticket booking system (BookMyShow LLD). Cover theaters, shows, seats, booking flow, and concurrent seat selection. Discuss locking strategy to prevent double booking.

prompts.title: STAR Method Coach
prompts.prompt: Act as a behavioral interview coach. Ask me a behavioral question (conflict, leadership, failure, or tight deadline). After I answer, evaluate my response using the STAR method and suggest improvements for clarity and impact.

prompts.title: Tell Me About Yourself
prompts.prompt: Help me craft a 2-minute 'Tell me about yourself' answer for an SDE intern role at a product company. My background: engineering student, DSA prep, 2 projects. Ask clarifying questions first, then draft and refine my pitch.

prompts.title: Failure & Learning Story
prompts.prompt: Help me prepare a 'Tell me about a failure' answer. Ask me about a real failure from academics or projects. Then shape it into a STAR response emphasizing ownership, learning, and concrete changes I made afterward.

prompts.title: Why This Company
prompts.prompt: I am interviewing at [COMPANY NAME]. Help me prepare a genuine 'Why this company?' answer. Ask me what I know about the company, then help me connect my skills, projects, and career goals to their product and culture.

prompts.title: Conflict Resolution Story
prompts.prompt: Coach me on answering 'Describe a conflict with a teammate.' Ask me for a real scenario. Help me structure it with STAR, focusing on empathy, communication, and outcome — not blaming others.
